triage.summary: Design trajectory to avoid singularity and mode switch for a six-axis arm performing a weld near wrist singularity; includes condition number threshold and velocity profile.

success_criteria: The offline trajectory file contains 901 waypoints at 1 mm spacing with the wrist reorientation ψ(s) = 12°·sin(π·s/900mm) applied, and evaluating κ(J) = σ_max/σ_min at every waypoint shows a maximum condition number of ≤ 8.0, with the worst-point value reported as ≤ 8.0 (design value 6.8 at s = 450 mm).

The velocity profile is implemented as a jerk-limited S-curve: 0→12 mm/s over 0.5 s, constant 12 mm/s, then 12→0 over 0.5 s, and every waypoint's computed joint velocity vector satisfies |q̇_i| ≤ 0.6·q̇_max,i for all six axes, with the maximum single-axis velocity at the worst point (s = 450 mm) documented and ≤ 30 deg/s.

All inverse-kinematics solutions in the trajectory keep every joint within ±120° on the primary axes (inside the ±170° physical limits) with no IK branch flip between consecutive waypoints (continuity check: |Δq| < 5° per 1 mm step).

The detection design defines three concrete layers written into the controller code: (1) plan-refusal if any waypoint κ > 8.0, (2) a 4 ms cyclic σ_min(J) monitor that executes a path-coherent 500 mm/s² deceleration stop when σ_min drops below 70% of planned, and (3) a joint-rate watchdog triggering a category-1 stop at 0.8·q̇_max.

Dry-run validation log over the full 76.8 s trajectory shows zero controller mode-switch events from Cartesian to joint interpolation and zero watchdog trips across 20 consecutive full-speed executions.

The implementation documents the condition number calculation κ(J) = ||J||₂·||J⁻¹||₂ = σ_max(J)/σ_min(J) with angular rows scaled by a 0.5 m characteristic length, and this same calculation is used consistently by the offline planner and the online monitor.
